chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad, from Asim, who said: A freedman of Salman narrated to me from 'Abidah al-Salmani, who said: I heard Ali (peace be upon him) saying:

"O people, fear Allah and do not give fatwa (juridical opinions) to people based on what you do not know, for indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said a statement that was altered by others to mean something else, and he said a statement: whoever places it in a position other than its proper place, he has lied against it."
So 'Abidah, 'Alqamah, and al-Aswad, and some others from them stood up and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what should we do with what has been reported to us in the Mushaf (Quran)?
He said: "The scholars of the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon them) are to be asked about that."

key_terms.عُلَمَاءُ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Scholars of the Family of Muhammad

ai.seo_question: How should one determine the correct interpretation of religious texts according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) warns against issuing fatwas based on ignorance, citing the Prophet’s caution that misplacing a statement constitutes a lie against him. When companions questioned how to reconcile their knowledge of the Quran with potential discrepancies, Ali directed them to consult the scholars of the Ahl al-Bayt, establishing their authority as the ultimate interpreters of divine text in Shia tradition.
